<!-- pr-reviewer: 9eee9c59dd9961e2c5befe4a4a597681863044cc -->
**Review: clean. Read, not built.** (A fork PR does not run on the self-hosted runner; the review is read-only.)

What was checked:

- The PR merges cleanly with main at this head (`mergeable: MERGEABLE`).
- The frame math is right: generate shifts a height by `h - origin.z` into the plane's frame; `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` back. `crates/app/tests/first_traverse.rs` pins both numbers in the user's frame (clearance 25, corner 25.209) and the raise (0.209 mm).
- The refusal law does not change. The same test asserts the post stays blocked and the refusal text carries the new message. The threshold keeps its local-frame values, so no verdict flips.
- `tilted` has `#[serde(default)]`; the old-cache load test and the serialize round trip pin it.
- Every match on `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` was checked: the two Display arms split on `tilted`; `job.rs`, `warned_moves.rs` and `ui/operations.rs` use `..` patterns, so none breaks.
- The tilted text has no Z value and no axis letters, per the plain-English rule. The upright text does not change.
- Commit ends with `Fixes #2991`; the body has a `Changelog:` line; the decision doc is in `docs/decisions/`; no process file changes.
- File lengths: all changed files stay under 400 lines. `types.rs` was already 471 lines on main; this PR adds 23. Noted, not blocked (pre-existing).

Labels: merge-ready set (read clean, mergeable). This work sits on the first-traverse gouge law (a refusal's reported heights); the coordinator's safety-floor second review applies before the merge.
